title: Unit – 5 : Session – 11 : SLO – 1  |  Initiating a Python Mini-Project on a Chosen Paradigm
sections: 1. Programming paradigm — a fundamental style/approach to structuring programs, e.g. imperative, object-oriented, functional, logic, event-driven or parallel programming.
2. Example mini-project — a Tkinter-based expense tracker using the event-driven paradigm (buttons trigger add/delete/report handlers), or a symbolic algebra quizzer using SymPy (symbolic paradigm).

3. Why choose a paradigm before coding — the paradigm shapes the architecture (classes vs pure functions vs event handlers), the libraries you need, and how testable/maintainable the result is; deciding early prevents mid-project rewrites and keeps the design coherent.
